newsitem.title: JAPAN: Basis for Japan recovery not eroded by tankan - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Basis for Japan recovery not eroded by tankan - BOJ.

text.p: The basis for Japan's economic recovery has not been eroded by the result of the "tankan" corporate survey, a senior Bank of Japan (BOJ) official told Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday.
"The basis for recovery has not been eroded in my opinion," said Kengo Inoue, an adviser to the BOJ governor.
He said investment plans of smaller firms had been revised upward and added that investment was spreading from major manufacturers to non-manufacturers and smaller firms.
Inoue also pointed to "fairly prolonged inventory adjustment" by the paper/pulp and steel industries "which is taking a much longer time than the two industries expected.
"That seems to be the major reason for this setback. Because as you can see, these major manufacturers were the only industry which saw a large setback," he said.

Asked about the possibility of improvements in these industries, Inoue said: "Well, (they) will probably have completed their inventory adjustment by the end of this year, so they will probably face somewhat better business conditions."

Asked when the yen's recent depreciation against the dollar would have an impact on business sentiment, he said this was difficult to determine. The BOJ said after releasing the tankan data that the yen's recent depreciation against the dollar was not adequately reflected in the survey.
Noting that the expected average exchange rate for this fiscal year was 102 yen to the dollar, Inoue said: "If the present rate stays, firms' profit picture could be slightly better."

The dollar has staged a gradual recovery from its post-war low of 79.75 yen, set in April 1995, and rose as far as 111.20 yen on July 8 this year. It stood at 108.40 yen in late Tokyo trade on Wednesday.
